### Data types

* [`Winget::Package`](#Winget--Package): Structured declaration of a single winget package.
Value type of `Winget::PackagesHash` (see `winget::packages`). Every key is
optional. `ensure`, `install_options`, `uninstall_options` and `schedule`
map to `package` resource attributes; `source`, `scope`, `architecture`,
`location`, `override`, `installer_type` and `locale` are translated into
`winget install`/`winget upgrade` flags; `hold` maps to the `mark`
property (`winget pin add` / `winget pin remove`); `allow_downgrade`
opts a pinned version in to the destructive uninstall-then-install
downgrade (provider strips the marker before calling winget).
* [`Winget::PackagesHash`](#Winget--PackagesHash): Hash of winget packages for `winget::packages`.
Keys are winget package IDs. Values are either a shorthand ensure string
(`'installed'`, `'latest'`, `'2.40.0'`, `'absent'`, ...) or a full
`Winget::Package` hash. Designed for Hiera (`winget::packages`, or
`winget::packages::entries` when declaring the sub-class directly):

```yaml
winget::packages:
  Git.Git:
    ensure: present
    scope: machine
  Microsoft.VisualStudioCode:
    ensure: latest
```

Named `PackagesHash` (rather than `Packages`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Packages` would collide
with the `winget::packages` class.
* [`Winget::SourceEntry`](#Winget--SourceEntry): Structured declaration of a single winget package source.
Value type of `Winget::SourcesHash` (see `winget::sources` and
`winget::source`). `url` maps to `winget source add --arg`; `source_type`
to `--type` (`Microsoft.PreIndexed.Package` or `Microsoft.Rest` for
private REST sources); `trust_level` to `--trust-level`; `explicit` to
`--explicit`; `header` to `--header` (REST source HTTP header, kept
`Sensitive` so it never lands in logs or reports).

Named `SourceEntry` (rather than `Source`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Source` would collide with
the `winget::source` defined type.
* [`Winget::SourcesHash`](#Winget--SourcesHash): Hash of winget package sources for `winget::sources`.
Keys are winget source names. Values are either a shorthand URL string
(added as a default source) or a full `Winget::SourceEntry` hash.
Designed for Hiera (`winget::sources`, or `winget::sources::entries`
when declaring the sub-class directly):

```yaml
winget::sources:
  contoso: https://winget.contoso.example.com/cache
  partners:
    url: https://winget.partners.example.com/cache
    source_type: Microsoft.Rest
    trust_level: trusted
```

Named `SourcesHash` (rather than `Sources`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Sources` would collide
with the `winget::sources` class.

## Classes

### <a name="winget"></a>`winget`

Ensures winget is available on the system so that the `winget` package provider can function.

=== Prerequisites

* Windows 10 version 1809 (build 17763) or later, Windows Server 2019 or later
* Internet access to download the App Installer package (or a local source via `source_path`)
* SYSTEM account must have read access to `%ProgramFiles%\WindowsApps`
* Proxy support via `proxy` parameter if the system requires a proxy for internet access

=== Usage

To ensure winget is installed with defaults:

  include winget

To install a specific version from a local source:

  class { 'winget':
    ensure      => '1.8.2391',
    source_path => 'C:\Sources\Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe.msixbundle',
  }

To guarantee ordering before packages using the winget provider:

  Class['winget'] -> Package <| provider == winget |>

=== Parameters

=== Ordering

Ordering with packages using the winget provider is done at the class level:

  Class['winget'] -> Package <| provider == winget |>

#### Examples

##### Manage packages from Hiera

```puppet
# hiera.yaml:
# winget::packages:
#   Git.Git:
#     ensure: present
#     scope: machine
include winget
```

##### <a name="-winget--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `String`

Desired state of winget. Valid values: 'present', 'absent', or a specific version string
(e.g., '1.8.2391'). Default: 'present' (installs latest available).

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DEPRECATED: Use `ensure` instead. Specific version to install (e.g., '1.8.2391').
This parameter is kept for backward compatibility.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--source"></a>`source`

Data type: `Enum['msstore', 'cdn', 'github', 'auto']`

Installation source for winget. Valid values: 'cdn' (Microsoft CDN
distribution of App Installer, preferred), 'github' (GitHub releases),
or 'auto' (tries cdn first, falls back to github). Default: 'auto'.
'msstore' is a deprecated alias for 'cdn' (same aka.ms/getwinget
download, not the Store app): it still works but logs a deprecation
warning, use 'cdn' instead. When a specific version is requested via
`ensure`/`version`, `auto` uses `github` directly: the Microsoft CDN
always serves the latest App Installer, so cdn cannot honor a pin.

Default value: `'auto'`

##### <a name="-winget--source_path"></a>`source_path`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Local filesystem path to a winget AppX/MSIX bundle file. When specified,
this takes precedence over `source`: only the local file is installed and
no `cdn`/`github` download is attempted. Use for offline installation.
The file must be a valid Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller package.

Default value: `undef`

Array of local AppX/MSIX files installed before the `source_path` bundle

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="winget--packages"></a>`winget::packages`

Reads package declarations from the `entries` hash (Hiera key
`winget::packages::entries`, see `Winget::PackagesHash`) and declares one
`package` resource with the winget provider per entry. The common case is
driven from the main class (`winget::packages` Hiera key, which declares
this class automatically): use `include winget`.
Entries accept either
a shorthand ensure string or a full `Winget::Package` hash:

- `ensure`, `install_options`, `uninstall_options` and `schedule` map to
  `package` resource attributes.
- `source`, `scope`, `architecture`, `location`, `override`,
  `installer_type` and `locale` are translated into `winget install` /
  `winget upgrade` flags (appended before any extra `install_options`).
- `hold` maps to the `mark` property, i.e. `winget pin add/remove` via the
  provider `holdable` feature (see `winget::pin` for blocking/gating pins).
- `allow_downgrade` opts a pinned version in to the destructive
  uninstall-then-install downgrade: `true` appends the string flag
  `'--allow-downgrade'` to `install_options` (stripped by the provider
  before calling winget; a string is required because the package type
  munges `install_options` hashes to String values only). Default/undef/false means no downgrade: an
  older plain-numeric pin falls back to `install --version` with a
  notice. Only pinned versions can downgrade (`ensure => latest` never
  does); suffixed versions never uninstall even with the opt-in.

A package already declared elsewhere in the catalog (e.g. `package {
'Git.Git': ensure => present }`) is left alone: redeclaring it would be a
duplicate-declaration error. Declare `winget::packages` after your own
`package` resources.

Scope note: the Puppet agent runs as SYSTEM. Packages installed with the
default (user) scope are invisible to `winget list` under SYSTEM, so prefer
`scope => 'machine'` for agent-managed packages (or set the matching
`installBehavior` preference via `winget::settings`).

Ordering with the bootstrap class is done at the call site:

  Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::packages']

#### Examples

##### Manage packages from Hiera (preferred)

```puppet
# hiera.yaml:
# winget::packages:
#   Git.Git:
#     ensure: present
#     scope: machine
#   Microsoft.VisualStudioCode:
#     ensure: '1.95.0'
#     hold: true
include winget
```

##### Manage packages via the sub-class directly

```puppet
# hiera.yaml:
# winget::packages::entries:
#   Git.Git:
#     ensure: present
#     scope: machine
include winget::packages
Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::packages']
```

##### Structured install parameters

```puppet
class { 'winget::packages':
  entries => {
    'Git.Git' => {
      ensure       => '2.44.0',
      scope        => 'machine',
      architecture => 'x64',
      source       => 'winget',
    },
  },
}
```

The following parameters are available in the `winget::packages` class:

* [`entries`](#-winget--packages--entries)
* [`schedule`](#-winget--packages--schedule)
* [`reboot_resource`](#-winget--packages--reboot_resource)

Data type: `Winget::PackagesHash`

Packages to manage, keyed by winget ID. Values are either a shorthand
ensure string or a `Winget::Package` hash.

##### <a name="-winget--packages--schedule"></a>`schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Default Puppet `schedule` applied as metaparameter to every managed
package. A per-package `schedule` key overrides it. Undef (default) means
no schedule: packages are enforced on every agent run.

Optional title of a `reboot` resource (puppetlabs/reboot, declared by the

by an installer (winget exit `0x8A150109`/`0x8A15010A`/`0x8A15010B`) is honored. Undef (default)
means no reboot wiring: installs still succeed with a warning, exactly
like the provider default.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="winget--settings"></a>`winget::settings`

Writes `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Packages/Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_*/LocalState/settings.json`
for the Puppet agent account (SYSTEM by default, i.e.
`C:/Windows/System32/config/systemprofile/...`), merging `config` with
`experimental_features` under the `experimentalFeatures` key. Hiera key
`winget::settings::config`. The common case is driven from the main class
(`winget::settings` Hiera key, which declares this class automatically). Accepts any
documented winget setting (`source.autoUpdateIntervalInMinutes`,
`installBehavior.preferences.scope`, `telemetry.disable`, ...): see
`winget settings` and https://aka.ms/winget-settings.

This is also where the fleet-wide install scope belongs: with the agent
running as SYSTEM, `installBehavior.preferences.scope => 'machine'` keeps
agent-driven installs visible to `winget list` without repeating
`scope => 'machine'` on every package (see `winget::packages`).

Nothing is managed while winget itself is absent (fresh bootstrap): order
settings after the bootstrap class (automatic when driven via `include
winget` with the `winget::settings` Hiera key):

  Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::settings']

The managed file is replaced wholesale on every run: `config` and
`experimental_features` are NOT merged with whatever settings.json
already contains on the node, they fully define its content. Declare
every key you care about (including ones a previous manual `winget
settings` edit may have set) or they will be dropped.

#### Examples

##### Disable telemetry and prefer machine scope

```puppet
class { 'winget::settings':
  config => {
    'telemetry'       => { 'disable' => true },
    'installBehavior' => { 'preferences' => { 'scope' => 'machine' } },
  },
}
```

##### Enable an experimental feature

```puppet
class { 'winget::settings':
  experimental_features => { 'resume' => true },
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::settings` class:

* [`config`](#-winget--settings--config)
* [`experimental_features`](#-winget--settings--experimental_features)
* [`settings_path`](#-winget--settings--settings_path)

##### <a name="-winget--settings--config"></a>`config`

Data type: `Hash`

Arbitrary settings.json content merged as-is (e.g.
`{ 'telemetry' => { 'disable' => true } }`).

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-winget--settings--experimental_features"></a>`experimental_features`

Data type: `Hash`

Experimental features merged under the `experimentalFeatures` key,
overriding any `experimentalFeatures` entry of `config`.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-winget--settings--settings_path"></a>`settings_path`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Explicit settings.json path (e.g. to manage another user's file).
Undef (default) manages the SYSTEM profile file used by the agent.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="winget--sources"></a>`winget::sources`

Reads source declarations from the `entries` hash (Hiera key
`winget::sources::entries`, see `Winget::SourcesHash`) and declares one
`winget::source` resource per entry. The common case is driven from the
main class (`winget::sources` Hiera key, which declares this class
automatically): use `include winget`.
Entries accept either a shorthand URL
string or a full `Winget::SourceEntry` hash (private REST sources, trust level,
explicit sources, auth headers).

With `reset_defaults => true`, non-default sources missing from `entries`
are removed first (`winget source reset --force`, idempotent guard included),
then the declared sources are added. The defaults themselves
(`msstore`, `winget`, `winget-font`, overridable via `default_sources`) are
never removed.

Nothing is declared while winget itself is absent (fresh bootstrap): order
sources after the bootstrap class so they converge on the next run:

  Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::sources']

#### Examples

##### Private REST source from Hiera (preferred)

```puppet
# hiera.yaml:
# winget::sources:
#   contoso:
#     url: https://winget.contoso.example.com/cache
#     source_type: Microsoft.Rest
#     trust_level: trusted
include winget
```

##### Private REST source via the sub-class directly

```puppet
# hiera.yaml:
# winget::sources::entries:
#   contoso:
#     url: https://winget.contoso.example.com/cache
#     source_type: Microsoft.Rest
#     trust_level: trusted
include winget::sources
Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::sources']
```

The following parameters are available in the `winget::sources` class:

* [`entries`](#-winget--sources--entries)
* [`reset_defaults`](#-winget--sources--reset_defaults)
* [`default_sources`](#-winget--sources--default_sources)

Data type: `Winget::SourcesHash`

Sources to manage, keyed by source name. Values are either a shorthand

Whether to reset winget sources to the defaults plus `entries`

### <a name="winget--upgrade"></a>`winget::upgrade`

Enumerates upgrade rows on demand through the `winget::upgrades` function
(one hash with `id`, `current_version` and `available_version` per
package) and declares one `package` resource with `ensure => latest`
(winget provider) per ID. Upgrades are
therefore regular Puppet resources (reporting, noop, `--tags`) instead of
an out-of-band scheduled task script.

Enumeration runs only when this class is declared: nodes without the class
never pay for a `winget upgrade` source round-trip. The opt-in
`winget_upgrades` fact (`WINGET_UPGRADES_ENABLED=true`) is only a fallback
for server-side compilation, where the function runs on the server without
winget, and standalone PuppetDB inventory. The function returns `undef`
when winget is absent or the query fails (fall back to the fact rows with
a warning) and `[]` only when the query succeeds with no rows (authoritative,
no fallback). A stale fact (e.g. TTL-cached)
is harmless: `ensure => latest` is idempotent, so IDs with no real upgrade
stay in sync.

Consent note: enumeration passes `--accept-source-agreements`, kept
deliberately so winget can never prompt (or stall where nothing answers)
on nodes that never opted in; the same flag is used by the provider and
the Bolt tasks for the upgrades applied here.

A package already declared elsewhere in the catalog (e.g. `package {
'Git.Git': ensure => present }`) is left alone: redeclaring it would be a
duplicate-declaration error. Such packages are therefore skipped here; to
upgrade them, either remove the other declaration or list the ID in
`exclude` and manage its upgrade yourself. Note the `defined()` guard only
sees resources parsed before this class, so declare `winget::upgrade`
after your own `package` resources (or rely on `exclude`).

A Puppet `schedule` metaparameter only skips the `package` resources outside
the window, it does not skip enumeration. When upgrades are confined to a
maintenance window, cache the opt-in fact with a TTL in facter.conf so the
inventory cost is paid at most once per window
(`facts: { ttls: [{ "winget_upgrades": "7 days" }] }`).

Ordering with the bootstrap class is done at the call site:

  Class['winget'] -> Class['winget::upgrade']

#### Examples

##### Upgrade everything on every run

```puppet
include winget::upgrade
```

##### Weekly window with exclusions, pins respected, reboot wired

```puppet
reboot { 'maintenance-reboot':
  when => pending,
}

class { 'winget::upgrade':
  exclude          => ['Google.Chrome'],
  manage_schedule  => true,
  schedule_period  => 'weekly',
  schedule_weekday => 'Sunday',
  schedule_range   => '3 - 5',
  reboot_resource  => 'maintenance-reboot',
}
```

##### Upgrade only selected packages, if installed

```puppet
class { 'winget::upgrade':
  only => ['Google.Chrome'],
}
# Hiera equivalent (automatic parameter lookup):
# winget::upgrade::only:
#   - Google.Chrome
# Absent IDs declare no resource and are never installed (unlike
# `package { ensure => latest }`), because IDs are matched against the
# on-demand enumeration which only lists installed packages.
```

##### Reuse a schedule declared elsewhere

```puppet
schedule { 'maintenance-window':
  period  => weekly,
  weekday => 'Sunday',
  range   => '3 - 5',
  repeat  => 1,
}

class { 'winget::upgrade':
  schedule => 'maintenance-window',
}
```

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Winget IDs never upgraded (case-insensitive).

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--only"></a>`only`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

When non-empty, upgrade only these winget IDs (case-insensitive).
Combined with `exclude`: an ID must be in `only` and not in `exclude`.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--respect_pins"></a>`respect_pins`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether pinned packages (`winget pin`, see the `winget_pins` fact and
`winget::pin`) are skipped. Default: true. This is the upgrade-side
counterpart of the provider `holdable` feature and is more robust than
`exclude` alone: pins travel with the node, not with this declaration.
Set to false to upgrade pinned packages explicitly.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--reboot_resource"></a>`reboot_resource`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional title of a `reboot` resource (puppetlabs/reboot, declared by the
caller) notified by every managed package, so a pending reboot requested
by an installer (winget exit `0x8A150109`/`0x8A15010A`/`0x8A15010B`) is honored. Undef (default)
means no reboot wiring: upgrades still succeed with a warning, exactly
like the provider default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule"></a>`schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Name of a Puppet `schedule` resource applied as metaparameter to every
managed package. Declare the resource yourself, or set `manage_schedule`
to have this class declare it. Undef (default) means no schedule: packages
are enforced on every agent run.
Note: this parameter intentionally shares its name with the Puppet
`schedule` metaparameter. In a resource-like class declaration (`class {
'winget::upgrade': schedule => '...', }`) the class parameter wins and is
forwarded as the metaparameter to the managed packages; this is covered
by unit tests on Puppet 7 and 8.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--manage_schedule"></a>`manage_schedule`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether this class declares `schedule { $schedule: ... }` from the
`schedule_*` parameters below.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule_name"></a>`schedule_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Name used for the managed schedule when `schedule` is undef.

Default value: `'winget-upgrade-window'`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule_period"></a>`schedule_period`

Data type: `Enum['hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly']`

`schedule` period.

Default value: `'weekly'`

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule_range"></a>`schedule_range`

Data type: `String[1]`

`schedule` range, e.g. `'3 - 5'` (03:00-05:00).

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule_weekday"></a>`schedule_weekday`

Data type: `String[1]`

`schedule` weekday, only used when `schedule_period` is `weekly`.

##### <a name="-winget--upgrade--schedule_repeat"></a>`schedule_repeat`

## Defined types

### <a name="winget--configure"></a>`winget::configure`

Applies a Desired State Configuration file (`.winget` / `.win-get.yaml`,
see `winget configure`) idempotently: the `exec` is skipped while
`winget configure test` reports the system in the desired state. Use this
for machine configuration winget handles natively (e.g. installing a tool
set alongside registry or package settings) instead of hand-rolled `exec`
resources.

Nothing is declared while winget itself is absent (fresh bootstrap): order
configurations after the bootstrap class:

  Class['winget'] -> Winget::Configure <| |>

#### Examples

##### Apply a baseline configuration

```puppet
winget::configure { 'C:/Configs/workstation.winget':
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::configure` defined type:

* [`source`](#-winget--configure--source)
* [`accept_configuration_agreements`](#-winget--configure--accept_configuration_agreements)

##### <a name="-winget--configure--source"></a>`source`

Data type: `String`

Path or HTTPS URL of the configuration file (`winget configure -f`).
Defaults to the resource title.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-winget--configure--accept_configuration_agreements"></a>`accept_configuration_agreements`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to pass `--accept-configuration-agreements`. Default: true
(required for non-interactive agent runs).

Default value: `true`

### <a name="winget--install--github"></a>`winget::install::github`

Installs winget from GitHub releases by downloading the AppX/MSIX bundle
and installing it with Add-AppxPackage. This is the recommended method for
pinning a specific winget version.

All commands run through the fully qualified PowerShell executable: the
`winget` alias is unavailable in the agent/SYSTEM context, so no bare
`winget` command is used here.

=== Parameters

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::install::github` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-winget--install--github--ensure)
* [`version`](#-winget--install--github--version)
* [`proxy`](#-winget--install--github--proxy)
* [`retry_count`](#-winget--install--github--retry_count)
* [`retry_interval`](#-winget--install--github--retry_interval)

##### <a name="-winget--install--github--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `String`

Desired state: 'present', 'absent', or a specific version string.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--install--github--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Specific version to install (e.g., '1.8.2391'). Defaults to latest release.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--install--github--proxy"></a>`proxy`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Proxy URL for the download.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--install--github--retry_count"></a>`retry_count`

Data type: `Integer`

Number of retry attempts for the installation. Default: 3.

Default value: `3`

##### <a name="-winget--install--github--retry_interval"></a>`retry_interval`

Data type: `Integer`

Seconds between retry attempts. Default: 10.

Default value: `10`

### <a name="winget--install--local"></a>`winget::install::local`

Installs winget from a local AppX/MSIX/MSIXBundle file. Use this for offline
installation where no internet access is available.

All commands run through the fully qualified PowerShell executable: the
`winget` alias is unavailable in the agent/SYSTEM context, so no bare
`winget` command is used here.

=== Parameters

* **Note** When `ensure` pins a version, the `source_path` bundle must contain
that version: the guard reinstalls while the installed version differs,
so a mismatching file would reinstall on every run.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::install::local` defined type:

* [`source_path`](#-winget--install--local--source_path)
* [`ensure`](#-winget--install--local--ensure)
* [`version`](#-winget--install--local--version)
* [`dependencies`](#-winget--install--local--dependencies)

##### <a name="-winget--install--local--source_path"></a>`source_path`

Data type: `String`

Required. Local filesystem path to the winget AppX/MSIX/MSIXBundle file.
Must be a valid Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller package.

##### <a name="-winget--install--local--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `String`

Desired state: 'present', 'absent', or a specific version string.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--install--local--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Specific version to install (e.g., '1.8.2391'). Recorded for interface
consistency; the installed version is determined by the file content.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--install--local--dependencies"></a>`dependencies`

Data type: `Array[String]`

Array of dependency AppX/MSIX files to install first. Optional.
Typically the VCLibs / UI.Xaml framework packages on offline hosts.

Default value: `[]`

### <a name="winget--install--msstore"></a>`winget::install::msstore`

Installs winget from the Microsoft CDN distribution of App Installer
(`https://aka.ms/getwinget`, a .msixbundle). This method is used instead of
the Microsoft Store app because it works in the SYSTEM context without the
Store and without an existing winget CLI, and it accepts the same proxy
settings as the other install methods.

Backs both `source => 'cdn'` (preferred) and `source => 'msstore'`
(deprecated alias) of the `winget` class: the download is the Microsoft
CDN in both cases, never the Store app.

The install runs only when App Installer is absent (presence guard): this
matters because the bundle version and the inner payload version can differ
(e.g. bundle 2026.728.x carrying a 1.29.290 payload), and Windows refuses
downgrades (0x80073D19), so reinstalling over a newer build would fail.

All commands run through the fully qualified PowerShell executable: the
`winget` alias is unavailable in the agent/SYSTEM context, so no bare
`winget` command is used here.

=== Parameters

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::install::msstore` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-winget--install--msstore--ensure)
* [`version`](#-winget--install--msstore--version)
* [`accept_source_agreements`](#-winget--install--msstore--accept_source_agreements)
* [`proxy`](#-winget--install--msstore--proxy)
* [`retry_count`](#-winget--install--msstore--retry_count)
* [`retry_interval`](#-winget--install--msstore--retry_interval)
* [`fail_on_error`](#-winget--install--msstore--fail_on_error)

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `String`

Desired state: 'present', 'absent', or a specific version string.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Accepted for interface consistency but ignored: the Microsoft CDN always
serves the latest App Installer. Pin a version with the `github` source
or a local file instead.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--accept_source_agreements"></a>`accept_source_agreements`

Data type: `Boolean`

Kept for interface consistency. Source agreements are implicitly accepted
by direct package installation.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--proxy"></a>`proxy`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Proxy URL for the download.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--retry_count"></a>`retry_count`

Data type: `Integer`

Number of retry attempts for the installation. Default: 3.

Default value: `3`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--retry_interval"></a>`retry_interval`

Data type: `Integer`

Seconds between retry attempts. Default: 10.

Default value: `10`

##### <a name="-winget--install--msstore--fail_on_error"></a>`fail_on_error`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether a failed install makes the catalog run fail. Default: true. Set
to false when another method acts as a fallback (`source => 'auto'`):
exit code 1 is then accepted, so the failure of this attempt does not
mark the including class as failed and the fallback still gets a chance.
Note that Puppet does not retry (`retry_count`) once exit code 1 is
accepted.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="winget--pin"></a>`winget::pin`

Manages `winget pin add/remove` for a single package ID. This covers the
advanced pin flavors the provider `holdable` feature (`mark => hold`, plain
pinning) does not: blocking pins (`blocking => true`, which also block
explicit `winget upgrade --id` unless `--force` is used) and gating pins
(`version => '1.2.*'`, which restrict upgrades to a version range).

A plain (non-blocking, unversioned) pin excludes the package from
`winget upgrade --all` while still allowing explicit upgrades, which is
exactly the `mark => hold` semantic; `winget::upgrade` additionally skips
pinned IDs automatically (`respect_pins`, backed by the `winget_pins` fact).
Do not combine a blocking pin with `ensure => latest` on the same package:
the explicit upgrade would fail until the pin is removed.

The pin presence guard is ID-based: changing `version` or `blocking` on an
existing pin requires removing it first (`ensure => absent`, then
`present` again).

Nothing is declared while winget itself is absent (fresh bootstrap): order
pins after the bootstrap class so they converge on the next run:

  Class['winget'] -> Winget::Pin <| |>

#### Examples

##### Hold back Chrome with a blocking pin

```puppet
winget::pin { 'Google.Chrome':
  ensure   => present,
  blocking => true,
}
```

##### Gate PowerToys to the 0.70 patch range

```puppet
winget::pin { 'Microsoft.PowerToys':
  ensure  => present,
  version => '0.70.*',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::pin` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-winget--pin--ensure)
* [`version`](#-winget--pin--version)
* [`blocking`](#-winget--pin--blocking)
* [`source`](#-winget--pin--source)

##### <a name="-winget--pin--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

Whether the pin exists (`present`) or not (`absent`).

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--pin--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional gating version (`'1.2.3'` or range `'1.2.*'`). Undef (default)
means a plain pin without version gating.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--pin--blocking"></a>`blocking`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the pin blocks even explicit upgrades. Default: false (plain
pinning: only `upgrade --all` skips the package).

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-winget--pin--source"></a>`source`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional source scoping the pin (`--source`). Undef (default) means all
sources.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="winget--source"></a>`winget::source`

Wraps `winget source add/remove` for one source (title is the source name).
This is how enterprise private sources (e.g. an internal
`Microsoft.Rest` source) are declared:

  winget::source { 'contoso':
    url         => 'https://winget.contoso.example.com/cache',
    source_type => 'Microsoft.Rest',
    trust_level => 'trusted',
  }

Nothing is declared while winget itself is absent (fresh bootstrap): order
sources after the bootstrap class so they converge on the next run:

  Class['winget'] -> Winget::Source <| |>

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `winget::source` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-winget--source--ensure)
* [`url`](#-winget--source--url)
* [`source_type`](#-winget--source--source_type)
* [`trust_level`](#-winget--source--trust_level)
* [`explicit`](#-winget--source--explicit)
* [`header`](#-winget--source--header)
* [`accept_source_agreements`](#-winget--source--accept_source_agreements)

##### <a name="-winget--source--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

Whether the source exists (`present`) or not (`absent`).

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-winget--source--url"></a>`url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Source URL or UNC (`winget source add --arg`). Required when
`ensure => present`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--source--source_type"></a>`source_type`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Source type (`winget source add --type`): `Microsoft.PreIndexed.Package`
(default) or `Microsoft.Rest`. Undef (default) lets winget decide.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--source--trust_level"></a>`trust_level`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['none', 'trusted']]`

Source trust level (`--trust-level`): `none` or `trusted`. Undef
(default) leaves the winget default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--source--explicit"></a>`explicit`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the source is explicit (`--explicit`): explicit sources must be
targeted with `--source` on every command. Default: false. Changing this
on an existing source is not enforced (remove and re-add instead).

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-winget--source--header"></a>`header`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

Optional REST source HTTP header (`--header`). `Sensitive` so the value
never lands in logs or reports.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-winget--source--accept_source_agreements"></a>`accept_source_agreements`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to pass `--accept-source-agreements` when adding the source.
Default: true (required for non-interactive agent runs).

Default value: `true`

## Functions

### <a name="winget--upgrades"></a>`winget::upgrades`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

On-demand winget upgrade inventory for `Class['winget::upgrade']`.

Runs `winget upgrade` once per compilation (memoized separately from the
gated fact cache, timeout-guarded by `PuppetX::Winget::Runner`) and returns
the same structured rows as the opt-in `winget_upgrades` fact: one hash
with `id`, `current_version` and `available_version` per upgradable
package. Returns `undef` when winget is absent or the query fails (so the
class can fall back to the fact rows); returns `[]` only when the query
succeeds with no rows. Never raises.

The class calls this function so enumeration happens only when the class
is declared. The fact rows (`$facts['winget_upgrades']`) are only a
fallback for server-side compilation (where this function runs on the
server without winget) and standalone PuppetDB inventory.

#### `winget::upgrades()`

On-demand winget upgrade inventory for `Class['winget::upgrade']`.

Runs `winget upgrade` once per compilation (memoized separately from the
gated fact cache, timeout-guarded by `PuppetX::Winget::Runner`) and returns
the same structured rows as the opt-in `winget_upgrades` fact: one hash
with `id`, `current_version` and `available_version` per upgradable
package. Returns `undef` when winget is absent or the query fails (so the
class can fall back to the fact rows); returns `[]` only when the query
succeeds with no rows. Never raises.

The class calls this function so enumeration happens only when the class
is declared. The fact rows (`$facts['winget_upgrades']`) are only a
fallback for server-side compilation (where this function runs on the
server without winget) and standalone PuppetDB inventory.

Returns: `Optional[Array[Hash]]` Upgrade rows with `id`, `current_version` and
`available_version` keys (`[]` on success with no rows, `undef` when
absent/error/disabled)

## Data types

### <a name="Winget--Package"></a>`Winget::Package`

Structured declaration of a single winget package.
Value type of `Winget::PackagesHash` (see `winget::packages`). Every key is
optional. `ensure`, `install_options`, `uninstall_options` and `schedule`
map to `package` resource attributes; `source`, `scope`, `architecture`,
`location`, `override`, `installer_type` and `locale` are translated into
`winget install`/`winget upgrade` flags; `hold` maps to the `mark`
property (`winget pin add` / `winget pin remove`); `allow_downgrade`
opts a pinned version in to the destructive uninstall-then-install
downgrade (provider strips the marker before calling winget).

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['ensure']            => Variant[Enum['present', 'installed', 'absent', 'purged', 'latest'], String[1]],
  Optional['source']            => String[1],
  Optional['scope']             => Enum['user', 'machine'],
  Optional['architecture']      => Enum['x86', 'x64', 'arm', 'arm64'],
  Optional['location']          => String[1],
  Optional['override']          => String[1],
  Optional['installer_type']    => String[1],
  Optional['locale']            => String[1],
  Optional['hold']              => Boolean,
  Optional['allow_downgrade']     => Boolean,
  Optional['install_options']   => Array,
  Optional['uninstall_options'] => Array,
  Optional['schedule']          => String[1],
}]
```

### <a name="Winget--PackagesHash"></a>`Winget::PackagesHash`

Hash of winget packages for `winget::packages`.
Keys are winget package IDs. Values are either a shorthand ensure string
(`'installed'`, `'latest'`, `'2.40.0'`, `'absent'`, ...) or a full
`Winget::Package` hash. Designed for Hiera (`winget::packages`, or
`winget::packages::entries` when declaring the sub-class directly):

```yaml
winget::packages:
  Git.Git:
    ensure: present
    scope: machine
  Microsoft.VisualStudioCode:
    ensure: latest
```

Named `PackagesHash` (rather than `Packages`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Packages` would collide
with the `winget::packages` class.

Alias of `Hash[String[1], Variant[String[1], Winget::Package]]`

### <a name="Winget--SourceEntry"></a>`Winget::SourceEntry`

Structured declaration of a single winget package source.
Value type of `Winget::SourcesHash` (see `winget::sources` and
`winget::source`). `url` maps to `winget source add --arg`; `source_type`
to `--type` (`Microsoft.PreIndexed.Package` or `Microsoft.Rest` for
private REST sources); `trust_level` to `--trust-level`; `explicit` to
`--explicit`; `header` to `--header` (REST source HTTP header, kept
`Sensitive` so it never lands in logs or reports).

Named `SourceEntry` (rather than `Source`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Source` would collide with
the `winget::source` defined type.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['ensure']                   => Enum['present', 'absent'],
  Optional['url']                      => String[1],
  Optional['source_type']              => String[1],
  Optional['trust_level']              => Enum['none', 'trusted'],
  Optional['explicit']                 => Boolean,
  Optional['header']                   => Sensitive[String[1]],
  Optional['accept_source_agreements'] => Boolean,
}]
```

### <a name="Winget--SourcesHash"></a>`Winget::SourcesHash`

Hash of winget package sources for `winget::sources`.
Keys are winget source names. Values are either a shorthand URL string
(added as a default source) or a full `Winget::SourceEntry` hash.
Designed for Hiera (`winget::sources`, or `winget::sources::entries`
when declaring the sub-class directly):

```yaml
winget::sources:
  contoso: https://winget.contoso.example.com/cache
  partners:
    url: https://winget.partners.example.com/cache
    source_type: Microsoft.Rest
    trust_level: trusted
```

Named `SourcesHash` (rather than `Sources`) because Puppet folds
definition names case-insensitively: `Winget::Sources` would collide
with the `winget::sources` class.

Alias of `Hash[String[1], Variant[String[1], Winget::SourceEntry]]`

## Tasks

### <a name="list_upgrades"></a>`list_upgrades`

List winget packages with available upgrades (read-only, makes no changes). For on-demand inventory outside Puppet agent runs.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `include_pinned`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

When false, exclude pinned packages from the listing. Default true: pinned packages are still listed.

### <a name="upgrade_now"></a>`upgrade_now`

Upgrade winget packages immediately (on-demand, outside Puppet agent runs). Upgrades the given IDs, or every package with an available upgrade when `ids` is empty.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `ids`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Winget IDs to upgrade. When empty, every package with an available upgrade is processed (minus `exclude`).

##### `exclude`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Winget IDs to skip (case-insensitive). Only used when `ids` is empty.

##### `include_pinned`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Also upgrade pinned packages when enumerating all upgrades. Explicit `ids` are always upgraded (a blocking pin still fails the package).
